title: Finite group quotients preserve relative projectivity
statement: Let $B$ be a Noetherian scheme quasi-projective over an affine Noetherian scheme, and let $V\to B$ be quasi-projective of finite type. Quasi-projective means admitting a locally closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the base. Let a finite group $H$ act on $V$ over $B$. Then there exists a categorical geometric quotient $q:V\to Q=V/H$ in schemes. The morphism $q$ is finite and surjective, its geometric fibres are the orbits, $\mathcal O_Q=(q_*\mathcal O_V)^H$, and $Q\to B$ is quasi-projective of finite type. If $V\to B$ is projective, then $Q\to B$ is projective in the finite-projective-space convention [def-kun-projective]. If $V$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], then $Q$ is integral. Restricting to any $H$-invariant open of $V$ gives its quotient as the corresponding open of $Q$. Finite morphisms and finite type are as in [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Categorical means that every $H$-invariant morphism from $V$ to a scheme factors uniquely through $q$.

source.place: WANTED locally. Rydh, Existence and properties of geometric quotients, arXiv:0708.3333v2, Theorem 4.4, Proposition 4.7, Remark 4.9, pp.20--23 (read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0708.3333). The ample-base hypothesis ensures that projectivity also has the finite-projective-space meaning.
